newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi sends Nigerian petrol back to Mozambique.
newsitem.headline: Malawi sends Nigerian petrol back to Mozambique.

text.p: More than 700,000 litres of petroleum from Nigeria estimated to cost seven million kwacha ($500,000) has been sent back to Beira in Mozambique after tested samples showed it was light petroleum and unsuitable for Malawian vehicles.

Petroleum Control Commission (PCC) General Manager Dennis Kambalame told Reuters on Monday that it was discovered the density for this supply was above normal and unsuitable for Malawian vehicles which use heavy petroleum.
"It was then discovered that the supply came from Nigeria," Kambalame said.
The Petrol Company of Mozambique supplies petroleum to Malawi's PCC.
Local newspaper Malawi News said over the weekend Malawi would experience a fuel shortage unless the supply was replenished within the shortest possible period.
But Kambalame dismissed fears that sending back more than 20 tankers with petroleum would bring fuel shortage in the country.
Land-locked Malawi's traditional supply routes include Beira and Nacala in Mozambique, Harare in Zimbabwe and Dar es Salaam in Tanzania.
